text: Asahna Bucha 2005: Thai Wikipedia's table says 20 July, my wan-phra says 21 July, and it is the only row before 2024 where we part. Which day did the temples keep?
The Thai calendar's full-moon day comes before the sky's full moon 242 times in 446 and after it only 11. Why one-sided? Measure where day 1 sits against the new moon.

A Royal Society of Thailand paper is said to count sabbaths running a day ahead of the Moon 24 and 34 times in B.E. 2556 and 2557. I only saw that through a search summary. Read it, and run my own count for those two years.
